tools.name: balance
tools.title: Read the prepaid balance
tools.description: The workspace's prepaid balance in USD, what runs in flight hold, what settled runs used today and this month (shown to the Owner), any daily spend cap on the team API key this connection uses, and where to top up. Check it when a run is refused for funds, or before a job that will make many runs. Free; changes nothing. NOT for: the price of one run, which is capability_inspect.

tools.name: capability_inspect
tools.title: Inspect and price a task or tool
tools.description: Read one task or provider tool from Ahel's catalog by its id: its exact inputs (Ahel's own contract, or the published reference input when Ahel has none), its status and exact reason, Ahel's price per provider (Unknown when Ahel has no rate), for a temporarily unavailable item the market prices seen elsewhere, for comparison, and the exact run_capability call when it can run. With arguments it also prices that exact run before anything runs: Ahel's quote, the most it may cost, the amount a run would reserve and whether the balance covers it; nothing is reserved, charged or started. With rows or rows_text (up to 100, for people.email.find or companies.register.search or companies.emails.from_website) it quotes a whole list instead: rows, rows that can run, each row's price and the most one row and the list may cost, the balance against it, and what each row that cannot run is missing. Free; changes nothing. NOT for: finding ids, which is capability_search, or running it, which is run_capability.

id.description: A task id or tool id from capability_search.

arguments.description: Optional: the run's inputs, by name, to price that exact run (a quote only; nothing runs).

max_items.description: With arguments: most rows to price for, 1-100. Default 10.

timeout_seconds.description: With arguments: longest the run may take, 1-180 seconds. Default: the provider's own (60, more for slow sources).

endpoint_ids.description: With arguments: price the run on these providers only (endpoint ids from this answer).

exclude_endpoint_ids.description: With arguments: price the run without these providers.

rows.description: A list for people.email.find or companies.register.search or companies.emails.from_website: 1 to 100 rows, each run once as its own run with its own exact cost. One object per row, such as {"name": "Patrick Collison", "domain": "stripe.com"} or {"name": "Wise", "country": "GB"}.

rows_text.description: A list for people.email.find or companies.register.search or companies.emails.from_website: 1 to 100 rows, each run once as its own run with its own exact cost. Instead of rows: paste up to 100 rows as text, one per line ("Patrick Collison, stripe.com"; "Wise, GB") or a CSV with a header row (name, domain, linkedin_url; name, country).

tools.name: capability_run_status
tools.title: Read a run's status and results
tools.description: Without execution_id: the paid data capabilities this workspace can run, each with its providers and exact prices. With execution_id: that run's state, attempts and exact cost, settled once in the ledger when final; with results true, its rows and provenance (include_raw true adds the provider's own answer), and, when it has rows, results_page and csv_url: give the person those links instead of writing the rows out again. Generated images and audio come as a signed link (media_url, valid for days) with their type and size; a small one is also attached as an image or audio block. A long result answers as many rows as fit and says the offset that reads the rest. NOT for: finding a task or tool to run, which is capability_search.

include_raw.description: With results: also include the winning provider's own answer (raw) and the normalised output. Large and repeats the rows; leave it out unless the rows lack a field you need.

offset.description: With results: the first row to answer (0-based), from next_offset when a long result did not fit in one answer. Default 0.

full_text.description: With results: answer long text values whole. By default a result of several rows cuts each text value at 4000 characters and lists the cut fields in that row's truncated_fields.

max_items.description: With results: the max_items the run was started with, so the answer can say when the rows stopped at that limit. run_capability's next names it.

tools.name: capability_search
tools.title: Search data tasks and provider tools
tools.description: Search Ahel's catalog of data tasks and provider tools by words, a task id or a tool id: company and people enrichment, SEO, social, ads, e-commerce, reviews, AI generation, market and public data. Each result has its genuine task id or tool id, its platform, its status (ready, coming_soon meaning temporarily unavailable because Ahel has no provider for it yet, or unavailable while the run service is down) with the exact reason; a temporarily unavailable result may carry a market price seen elsewhere, for comparison. The same catalog, ids and statuses as the Catalog page on ahel.ai. Describe the job in plain words; results are ranked by how well they fit. When nothing fits it answers verdict none with the three nearest items: then call catalog_request. Free; changes nothing. NOT for: one item's exact inputs and prices, which is capability_inspect, or the team's own tools, which is my_tools.

query.description: Words to match, or an exact task id (companies.enrich) or tool id.

platform.description: Optional platform id (companies, google, image-gen): only its items; with no query, its whole shelf.

kind.description: Optional: only tasks or only provider tools.

status.description: Optional: only items in this state.

tools.name: catalog_request
tools.title: Request a missing task or tool
tools.description: Ask Ahel to add a data task or provider tool the catalog does not have yet: call it when capability_search answers verdict none and none of its nearest items fits. Give what you need in plain words, an example input, and the most you would pay for one call. Answers a request id; asking again for the same thing adds to that request instead of making a new one. Free; runs nothing and charges nothing. NOT for: finding what already exists, which is capability_search.

what.description: What you need done, in plain words: the job, not a provider name.

example_input.description: Optional: one example input, as text or an object (a domain, a profile URL, a name).

max_price_usd.description: Optional: the most you would pay for one call, in USD.

tools.name: feedback
tools.title: Rate a run or report a problem
tools.description: Rate one run or one catalog request of this workspace good or bad, or, with no id, report anything about Ahel: confusing results or charges, unclear instructions, unhelpful errors, a workaround you needed. Report small annoyances too, even when the task succeeded, each issue once. Ahel reads every note to fix providers and the catalog. Leave out private information, keys and raw responses. Free; changes nothing else. NOT for: reading a run's state or rows, which is capability_run_status, or asking for a missing task, which is catalog_request.

id.description: To rate one: an execution id from run_capability, or a request id from catalog_request.

category.description: With no id: quality (results), pricing (charges or prices), friction (using Ahel) or other.

note.description: What was right or wrong, in a sentence or two. Required with no id.

tools.name: get_started
tools.title: Get started with Ahel
tools.description: How to start with Ahel: call this when the person asks what Ahel is, what it can do or how to begin. Returns what Ahel is, how the prepaid balance works, the three steps to find, price and run any data task or provider tool, and ready example prompts. Reads only; changes nothing. NOT for: finding a data task or provider tool for a specific ask, which is capability_search.

tools.name: my_tools
tools.title: List or call the team's own tools
tools.description: This team's own tools: the APIs and MCP servers the team added at ahel.ai/app/tools. Without tool, lists each one with its tools, their inputs and the exact call. With tool ("<key>/<tool name>" from that list) and arguments, calls it with the team's saved credentials, which never enter the chat. NOT for: Ahel's catalog of data tasks and provider tools, which is capability_search. If the transport times out, do not resubmit the work: call again with the same ids and poll.

tool.description: Optional: "<key>/<tool name>" from the list, to call that tool. Omit to list the team's own tools.

arguments.description: With tool: the tool's arguments, matching the inputs the list shows.

tools.name: review
tools.title: Review a run's usefulness
tools.description: Rate how useful one finished run of this workspace was, after you have used its result: useful, partly, not_useful, or not_sure when you cannot tell, with an optional reason about the result (missing rows, wrong data, stale). One review per run; reviewing it again replaces the earlier one. Ahel reads every review to rank and fix providers. Leave out private information, keys and raw rows. Free; changes nothing else. NOT for: a catalog request, or reporting something confusing or broken, which is feedback.

reason.description: Optional: why, in a sentence or two, about the result.

tools.name: run_batch
tools.title: Run one task over many inputs
tools.description: Run one task over many inputs in one call: for repeated runs of the same task, one round trip rather than one per run. Priced the same per item as a single run, with no fee for batching: each item is quoted, reserved and charged on its own, and only a delivered result is charged. Give id and items, 1 to 100 objects of the task's inputs. Every item is checked first: a bad item is refused alone and the others run. Identical items run once and the answer maps back to each position. At most 5 run at once. max_cost_usd caps the whole batch: no item starts if what is charged, plus what is held, plus its own quote could pass it, and items left over answer not_started with nothing charged. A provider that is temporarily unavailable stops only the items it would serve. The answer comes within about 45 seconds: each item in input order has its position, state, rows, charged_usd, error and execution_id, then the totals. Items still going, and rows that did not fit, are read with capability_run_status. An item with rows also has results_page and csv_url: give the person those links instead of writing the rows out again. Sending the same call again the same UTC day answers the same runs with no new charge and starts what did not start; a new idempotency_key runs the items again. A task that is unknown or not ready refuses the whole call, free. NOT for: one run alone, which is run_capability.

id.description: A task id or tool id from capability_search or capability_inspect. One task for the whole batch.

items.description: 1 to 100 objects, each the task's inputs for one run, by name, as run_capability's arguments.

max_items.description: Most rows each item collects, 1-100. Default 10.

max_cost_usd.description: Optional: the most the whole batch may cost, in USD, such as "2.50". Without it the workspace's normal limits apply.

idempotency_key.description: Optional: your own key for this batch, 8 to 200 letters, digits, dots, underscores, colons or hyphens. The same key and item answers the same run with no new charge; a new key runs it again. Left out, the same call the same UTC day is the same batch.

tag.description: Optional: a label for every run in this batch, such as the customer or project it is for: 1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores. Activity shows runs and cost by tag. It stays in Ahel and is never sent to a provider.

tools.name: run_capability
tools.title: Run a paid data task
tools.description: Run one paid data capability (company data, people and contact data and the like) through Ahel's provider execution: it is quoted, the exact price is reserved from the workspace balance, and the run starts. Give id, a task id or tool id from capability_search: it runs only through the v2 capability Ahel's task map binds to it, and an item that is not ready is refused with its exact reason before anything is quoted. It then waits up to wait_seconds (default 20, at most 50; 0 answers at once): when the run finishes in that time, this same answer has its state, exact cost and rows, and generated images and audio as links; otherwise it answers the execution id, and capability_run_status reads the run. An answer with rows also has results_page and csv_url: give the person those links instead of writing the rows out again. Data collection only: a capability that writes or has a side effect is refused. Ahel picks the provider unless endpoint_ids pins one; exclude_endpoint_ids leaves providers out. Give max_cost_usd to hold the price: a run that would cost more is refused with nothing run or charged. Give idempotency_key so a retry after a lost answer is safe: the same key answers the same run, with no new charge. Give tag (such as a customer name) to see usage and cost by tag in Activity. A list: for people.email.find or companies.register.search or companies.emails.from_website, give rows (objects) or rows_text (paste up to 100 rows as text) instead of arguments: without confirm it answers the list's quote and runs nothing; with confirm true it runs every row once and answers the receipt (found, not found, failed, the exact total, the rows and a CSV link) and its run_id; run_id continues a run whose rows were still going. NOT for: the team's own tools, which is my_tools.

id.description: A task id or tool id from capability_search or capability_inspect.

capability_id.description: Instead of id: a v2 capability id from capability_run_status (no execution_id).

arguments.description: The capability's inputs, by name. Required unless rows, rows_text or run_id is given; with a list, {"verify": true} checks every found email.

timeout_seconds.description: Longest the run may take, 1-180 seconds. Default: the provider's own (60, more for slow sources).

endpoint_ids.description: Optional: run only on these providers, by the endpoint ids capability_inspect lists. Leave it out to let Ahel pick (the default).

exclude_endpoint_ids.description: Optional: never use these providers, by the endpoint ids capability_inspect lists. Ahel picks among the rest.

max_cost_usd.description: Optional: the most this run may cost, in USD, such as "0.05". capability_inspect's next names the quoted maximum. Ahel uses only providers that fit under it, and when none does the run is refused with nothing run or charged. One run only; a list has its own quote and confirm.

wait_seconds.description: Optional: how long to wait for the run to finish and answer its rows here, 0-50 seconds. Default 20; 0 answers the execution id at once. A list waits up to 45 s.

idempotency_key.description: Optional: your own key for this run, 8 to 200 letters, digits, dots, underscores, colons or hyphens. Sending the same call again with the same key answers the same run with no new charge; the same key with different inputs is refused.

tag.description: Optional: a label for this run, such as the customer or project it is for: 1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores. Activity shows runs and cost by tag. It stays in Ahel and is never sent to a provider.

rows.description: A list for people.email.find or companies.register.search or companies.emails.from_website: 1 to 100 rows, each run once as its own run with its own exact cost. One object per row, such as {"name": "Patrick Collison", "domain": "stripe.com"} or {"name": "Wise", "country": "GB"}.

rows_text.description: A list for people.email.find or companies.register.search or companies.emails.from_website: 1 to 100 rows, each run once as its own run with its own exact cost. Instead of rows: paste up to 100 rows as text, one per line ("Patrick Collison, stripe.com"; "Wise, GB") or a CSV with a header row (name, domain, linkedin_url; name, country).

confirm.description: With rows or rows_text: true runs the list once the person agrees to its quote. Left out, the answer is the quote and nothing runs. The same list sent again the same UTC day answers the first run's receipt and neither runs nor charges again; a new idempotency_key runs it again.

run_id.description: With id: the run_id a list's receipt answered, to read its rows still running and start the rest. Rows already run are never run twice.
